The family registry: the ONE place model families are enumerated.

Every supported HuggingFace architecture is described by a `FamilySpec`
— a frozen value object holding the family key, the HF `model_type` values it
covers, and the four functions a family module must implement:

```
canonicalize_weights(cfg, raw) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]
param_specs(cfg)               -> dict[str, evoxc.TensorSpec]
graph(cfg, seq_len, batch_size=1, *, pack_plan=None) -> @evoxc.defn forward
reference(cfg, params, input_ids) -> np.ndarray
```

Adding a family is **one module plus one entry in** `FAMILIES` — nothing
else in the package needs to change (`evoxc_hf.program` /
`evoxc_hf.pipeline` and the public API read the registry, they never
hard-code a family). The two v1 families live in `evoxc_hf.models.llama` and
`evoxc_hf.models.gpt2`.

Two invariants are enforced at *import* time, so a drifted registry fails loudly
instead of silently mis-routing a checkpoint:

* every `FamilySpec.name` equals its key in `FAMILIES` and the source
  module's `FAMILY` attribute;
* the per-family `model_types` are derived from
  `evoxc_hf.config.FAMILY_BY_MODEL_TYPE` and must agree with a family
  module's own `MODEL_TYPES` tuple when the module declares one.

Import-time constraint: this module imports only the family modules (which
import `numpy` / `evoxc` — both hard dependencies) and
`evoxc_hf.config` / `evoxc_hf.errors`. It must never import torch,
transformers, safetensors or iree, so `import evoxc_hf` stays numpy-only.
